steps: The variety of organisms in ecosystems is called biodiversity.
items.finalAnswer: Biodiversity is the variety of organisms in ecosystems.

steps: Biodiversity provides humans with food, medicines, fuel and other useful products.
Different organisms provide important ecosystem services, such as pollination and the maintenance of soil fertility.
Biodiversity helps maintain the balance and stability of ecosystems on Earth.
items.finalAnswer: Biodiversity provides useful resources and ecosystem services, and helps maintain the balance of life on Earth.

steps: The seven taxonomic ranks in the Linnaean system, from the largest group to the smallest, are:
Kingdom
Phylum (division in plants)
Class
Order
Family
Genus
Species
items.finalAnswer: Kingdom, phylum (division), class, order, family, genus and species.

steps: Lion: Kingdom Animalia; Phylum Chordata; Class Mammalia; Order Carnivora; Family Felidae; Genus Panthera; Species Panthera leo.
Corn: Kingdom Plantae; Division Magnoliophyta; Class Liliopsida; Order Poales; Family Poaceae; Genus Zea; Species Zea mays.
items.finalAnswer: Lion: Animalia, Chordata, Mammalia, Carnivora, Felidae, Panthera, Panthera leo. Corn: Plantae, Magnoliophyta, Liliopsida, Poales, Poaceae, Zea, Zea mays.

steps: Archaea and bacteria are both unicellular prokaryotes, but they differ in some important features.
The cell walls of bacteria contain peptidoglycan; archaeal cell walls do not contain peptidoglycan.
Archaeal cell membranes have distinctive branched lipids, unlike the membrane lipids of bacteria.
Some archaea live in extreme environments, although archaea also live in ordinary environments.
items.finalAnswer: Archaea differ from bacteria in cell-wall composition and membrane lipids; some archaea also live in extreme environments.

steps: The three-kingdom system did not clearly distinguish organisms with prokaryotic cells from those with eukaryotic cells.
It placed fungi in the plant kingdom, although fungi do not have chlorophyll and obtain food heterotrophically.
The kingdom Protista contained very different organisms, including unicellular organisms and organisms with different modes of nutrition.
items.finalAnswer: The system did not separate prokaryotes from eukaryotes, grouped fungi with plants, and placed diverse organisms together in Protista.

steps: The kingdom Animalia includes multicellular, heterotrophic organisms that lack cell walls.
Fungi are eukaryotic organisms; they may be unicellular or multicellular.
They lack chlorophyll and obtain food heterotrophically by absorption.
Their cell walls are made of chitin.
The body of a multicellular fungus consists of thread-like hyphae, which form a mycelium.
Fungi commonly reproduce by spores.
items.finalAnswer: Fungi are eukaryotic, chlorophyll-lacking heterotrophs with chitin cell walls; many have hyphae forming a mycelium and reproduce by spores.
